## Scope and plan revision

State whether this change touches anything the plan fixes. Each item below is a **plan revision**, not an
implementation choice: raise it in this description so the decision is discussed once instead of
reconstructed from a diff, rather than folding it into a feature change.

- [ ] None of the items below is touched, or the one that is is described here:
- [ ] An **append-only store** — `standard_versions`, `evaluation_reports`, `report_case_results`,
      `governance_events`, `ledger_entries`, `transactions`, `refunds`, `audit_events` or
      `listing_versions`. A route may insert a row in one and may never update or delete one.
- [ ] A **status code** the API contract documents: `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `422` or `429`.
- [ ] A **fixed interface**: the Shield decision result of `evaluate(call, policy, context)` returning
      `allow`, `deny` or `needs_approval` with its reason and rule ID; the report shape; the badge
      vocabulary; the pass rule of `SGI-SO-1.0.0` (at least 18 of 20 cases match and no `critical` case
      fails); or the endpoint contract.
- [ ] A **migration file** under `packages/shared/migrations/`. An applied migration is immutable — the
      runner records its checksum and refuses to start when the file's bytes changed — and migrations
      only add; none drops or rewrites.
- [ ] A **workspace or path** in the repository tree. Files may be added inside the listed directories;
      no workspace may be added and no listed path may be moved.

## Verification

Run these and paste what they printed. CI runs `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:e2e`,
`npm run test:a11y`, `npm run scan:exclusions` and `npm run deps:report` in that order, so a green run
covers the same ground — say so if CI is what ran them.

- [ ] `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` exit 0.
- [ ] `npm test` — unit tests, integration tests and the exclusion scan's self-test. Observed:
- [ ] `npm run test:e2e` — the developer-to-buyer loop and the page walk. Observed:
- [ ] `npm run test:a11y` — 1280 px and 360 px, for a change that renders. Observed:
- [ ] `npm run scan:exclusions` — paste the output. On this repository it is an empty finding list with
      exit 0; list anything it found, with its file and line.
- [ ] `npm run deps:report` — paste the output, and confirm that `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` is regenerated
      and committed with this change, or state that it is unchanged because no manifest changed. It is
      generated output and is never hand-edited.

The one-time `npx playwright install chromium` is the only network step the project needs, and `README.md`
documents it; nothing else here reaches a service, an account or a credential.

## Pre-pull-request artefacts

Three artefacts ride with this description, not three sentences about them.

- [ ] The `npm run scan:exclusions` output, pasted above.
- [ ] `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`, regenerated by `npm run deps:report` in this same change.
- [ ] `docs/REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md`, completed with one sign-off line per category — personal names;
      contextual disclosure of private or nonpublic information; references to private projects,
      products or datasets — for any change that touches UI text, seed data, fixtures, documentation,
      comments or examples.

The manual review is not replaced by the scan. The scan matches patterns rather than meaning: it detects
mail-address patterns, telephone-number patterns, credential material and prohibited dependency names,
and nothing else. A clean run is supplementary to the manual review, and it must never be described as
guaranteeing the absence of private information.

## Repository rules

- [ ] One logical change, on a branch named `type/short-description`, with an imperative commit subject
      under 72 characters and a pull-request title in the imperative mood.
- [ ] No personal information, contact detail, financial information, credential, token or secret was
      introduced — and none is needed, because the product requires no secret and no environment variable.
- [ ] No dependency was added outside the closed inventory. If one was, its exact version, licence and
      purpose were recorded in the inventory first, its purpose record is in `scripts/deps-report.ts`,
      and its licence passes the allowlist data in `scripts/license-allowlist.json`. Read that data file:
      it is the list the gate applies, and it carries the development-only exceptions — `MPL-2.0` among
      them — which may never appear in a runtime graph.
- [ ] No real payment path, no payment provider's name, no production authentication, no real personal
      data, no execution of third-party code and no personalised advertising or tracking was introduced.
      All of them are deferred or forbidden, and they are declined at the source.
- [ ] The label vocabulary is intact and nothing beyond it was added: `SAMPLE` or `VERIFIED-IN-DEMO` on a
      report, `Sponsored` on a sponsored item, `DEMO` on a simulated amount, `demo only, no production
      authentication` on a demo session, `No SGI report yet` for a listing with no evaluation, and
      `to be determined` for the founder-allocation contract structure. No claim of certification,
      independent verification, universal safety or a guaranteed pass was added.
- [ ] Trust separation holds: nothing carries fee, sponsorship or commercial data into scoring, a report,
      a badge or the organic ordering of a listing.
- [ ] Files sit where the tree says they sit: source files kebab-case, types PascalCase, exactly one
      `index.ts` public entry per workspace, a unit test beside its source as `<name>.test.ts`,
      integration tests in `apps/api/test/integration/`, end-to-end and accessibility tests in `e2e/`.
- [ ] A change to a protected path asks for a maintainer's review in this description, and a change to a
      fixed interface, a status code or the append-only set is flagged in the Scope section above.
